wins.text: Q4 revenue of $39.3B, up 78% YoY and 12% sequentially, beating the $37.5B outlook; FY2025 revenue of $130.5B, up 114% YoY
Data Center revenue of $35.6B in Q4, up 93% YoY and 16% sequentially — a record; FY2025 Data Center revenue of $115.2B, more than doubling YoY
Blackwell delivered $11B in revenue in Q4, described as the fastest product ramp in company history, exceeding internal expectations
Automotive revenue hit a record $570M in Q4, up 103% YoY and 27% sequentially; FY2025 automotive revenue of $1.7B up 55% YoY, with $5B guided for FY2026
Returned $8.1B to shareholders via share repurchases and cash dividends in Q4

risks.text: Non-GAAP gross margins of 73.5% declined sequentially and are guided to remain in the low 70s during Blackwell ramp, with Q1 guided at 71% non-GAAP — a meaningful step down from prior mid-70s levels
Gaming revenue of $2.5B declined 22% sequentially and 11% YoY due to supply constraints, though management expects recovery in Q1

China data center revenue remains well below pre-export-control levels at roughly half of prior share, with management flagging a 'very competitive' market and no expected recovery absent regulatory change
Tariff impact on semiconductors acknowledged as 'unknown' by CFO, with timing, scope, and magnitude still unclear — a potential headwind to gross margin trajectory
Networking revenue declined 3% sequentially as the company transitions from NVLink 8/InfiniBand to NVLink 72/Spectrum-X architecture, creating a near-term revenue gap

guidance_items.detail: Q1 FY2026 revenue guided to $43B +/- 2%, well above Q4 actual of $39.3B and prior $37.5B Q4 guide
Q1 non-GAAP gross margin guided to 71% +/- 50bps, down from Q4 actual of 73.5%; expected to remain in low 70s during Blackwell ramp before recovering to mid-70s later in FY2026
Sequential growth expected in both Data Center (compute and networking) and Gaming in Q1
FY2026 operating expenses expected to grow to mid-30s as a percentage; Automotive revenue expected to grow to ~$5B in FY2026
Q1 GAAP operating expenses ~$5.2B, non-GAAP ~$3.6B; full-year opex growth guided to mid-30s range

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Custom ASIC competition and heterogeneous supercluster architectures as an alternative to merchant GPUs
Hopper-era infrastructure replacement/refresh cycle timing and whether installed base creates upgrade headwinds
Geographic concentration risk — whether U.S. demand alone can sustain growth if other regions face export restrictions
